## Completed example

**Decision ID and date:** METH-004, 28 August 2026
**Research question:** Can enrolment records identify candidates at elevated near-term withdrawal risk within University X?
**Intended inference:** predictive discrimination and calibration in a defined historical institutional cohort.
**Chosen design:** retrospective temporal validation using administrative records.

| Link | Decision | Threat |
|---|---|---|
| Target | enrolled candidates in 2021–2025 under the recorded policy system | not transportable to other institutions or policy periods |
| Source | institutional enrolment and milestone records | missing or administrative coding may reflect process rather than candidate state |
| Measurement | withdrawal within twelve months using verified status history | transfers and interruptions may be misclassified |
| Analysis | time-separated training and validation with calibration reporting | drift and small event counts |
| Claim | bounded prediction, no causal language | users may interpret risk score as cause or destiny |

**Rejected alternative:** causal analysis; no defensible identification strategy is currently available.
**Pilot:** manually reconcile a stratified sample of outcome histories before modelling.
**Stop condition:** the outcome date cannot be reconstructed reliably or lawful access conditions prohibit the proposed use.
**Next review:** after outcome audit and data-governance confirmation.

## Scenario test

The pilot shows that an important measure is unreliable. Do not edit the decision record to make the original choice appear sound. Append the evidence, mark the affected link, and record whether the project will repair the measure, narrow the claim, change design, pause or stop.
